messages.subject: stacked bars, multiple layers + legend
parts:
Trying to do a bar chart with 

- change in GDP
- stacked contributions to GDP

I tried to do it with 3 layers
- GDP bars
- stacked positive contributions to GDP
- stacked negative contributions to GDP

It worked more or less OK until I tried to customize the legend, when I did that it went haywire. Got multiple legends, presumably for multiple layers. Also not sure if scale_colour_manual will let you specify color and fill independently for bars. Any way to make only the custom legend appear and fix the colors?

Not sure if I'm going about this all wrong, or if it's a bug or limitation, or missing something simple. Any pointers greatly appreciated.

library(quantmod)
library(ggplot2)
library(tis)

# get data statement
getSymbols("GDPC96", src="FRED")
getSymbols("PCECC96", src="FRED")
getSymbols("FPIC96", src="FRED")
getSymbols("CBIC96", src="FRED")
getSymbols("GCEC96", src="FRED")
getSymbols("NETEXC96", src="FRED")

# compute values
GDPC96_comp = GDPC96 - lag(GDPC96,1)
PCECC96_comp = PCECC96 - lag(PCECC96,1)
FPIC96_comp = FPIC96 - lag(FPIC96,1)
CBIC96_comp = CBIC96 - lag(CBIC96,1)
GCEC96_comp = GCEC96 - lag(GCEC96,1)
NETEXC96_comp = NETEXC96 - lag(NETEXC96,1)

# truncate
GDPC96_comp = GDPC96_comp['2008::']
PCECC96_comp = PCECC96_comp['2008::']
FPIC96_comp = FPIC96_comp['2008::']
CBIC96_comp = CBIC96_comp['2008::']
GCEC96_comp = GCEC96_comp['2008::']
NETEXC96_comp = NETEXC96_comp['2008::']

# make dataframe for pos values
PCECC96_pos<-PCECC96_comp['2008::']
PCECC96_pos[PCECC96_pos<0]<-0
FPIC96_pos<-FPIC96_comp['2008::']
FPIC96_pos[FPIC96_pos<0]<-0
CBIC96_pos<-CBIC96_comp['2008::']
CBIC96_pos[CBIC96_pos<0]<-0
GCEC96_pos<-GCEC96_comp['2008::']
GCEC96_pos[GCEC96_pos<0]<-0
NETEXC96_pos<-NETEXC96_comp['2008::']
NETEXC96_pos[NETEXC96_pos<0]<-0

PCECC96_posframe<-data.frame(PCECC96_pos)
PCECC96_posframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(PCECC96_posframe))
FPIC96_posframe<-data.frame(FPIC96_pos)
FPIC96_posframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(FPIC96_posframe))
CBIC96_posframe<-data.frame(CBIC96_pos)
CBIC96_posframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(CBIC96_posframe))
GCEC96_posframe<-data.frame(GCEC96_pos)
GCEC96_posframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(GCEC96_posframe))
NETEXC96_posframe<-data.frame(NETEXC96_pos)
NETEXC96_posframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(NETEXC96_posframe))

posframe <- PCECC96_posframe
posframe <- merge(posframe, FPIC96_posframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
posframe <- merge(posframe, CBIC96_posframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
posframe <- merge(posframe, GCEC96_posframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
posframe <- merge(posframe, NETEXC96_posframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
#fix dates to center quarters
posframe$date= posframe$date + 60

posmelt <- melt(posframe, id = 'date')

# make dataframe for neg values

PCECC96_neg<-PCECC96_comp['2008::']
PCECC96_neg[PCECC96_neg>0]<-0
FPIC96_neg<-FPIC96_comp['2008::']
FPIC96_neg[FPIC96_neg>0]<-0
CBIC96_neg<-CBIC96_comp['2008::']
CBIC96_neg[CBIC96_neg>0]<-0
GCEC96_neg<-GCEC96_comp['2008::']
GCEC96_neg[GCEC96_neg>0]<-0
NETEXC96_neg<-NETEXC96_comp['2008::']
NETEXC96_neg[NETEXC96_neg>0]<-0

PCECC96_negframe<-data.frame(PCECC96_neg)
PCECC96_negframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(PCECC96_negframe))
FPIC96_negframe<-data.frame(FPIC96_neg)
FPIC96_negframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(FPIC96_negframe))
CBIC96_negframe<-data.frame(CBIC96_neg)
CBIC96_negframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(CBIC96_negframe))
GCEC96_negframe<-data.frame(GCEC96_neg)
GCEC96_negframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(GCEC96_negframe))
NETEXC96_negframe<-data.frame(NETEXC96_neg)
NETEXC96_negframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(NETEXC96_negframe))

negframe <- PCECC96_negframe
negframe <- merge(negframe, FPIC96_negframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
negframe <- merge(negframe, CBIC96_negframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
negframe <- merge(negframe, GCEC96_negframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
negframe <- merge(negframe, NETEXC96_negframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
#fix dates to center quarters
negframe$date= negframe$date + 60

negmelt <- melt(negframe, id = 'date')

gdpframe<-data.frame(GDPC96_comp['2008::'])
gdpframe$date<-as.Date(rownames(gdpframe))+30
gdpmelt <- melt(gdpframe, id = 'date')

fullframe <- merge(negframe, posframe, by.x="date", by.y="date", all=TRUE)
fullmelt <- melt(fullframe, id = 'date')

# sort of OK without explicit legend params
ggp = ggplot(data=fullmelt, aes(x=date, y=value, color=variable, fill=variable, width=20)) + 
    scale_x_date(expand = c(0, 0)) + 
    xlab("
Source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis") + 
    ylab("$billions 2005 dollars") + 
    theme_bw() +
    layer(data=gdpmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=posmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=negmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    opts(legend.position="top", legend.direction="horizontal", plot.background = theme_rect(colour = 'black', fill = '#CCCCEE', size = 1, linetype='solid'))

#output 
png(filename="/Temp/contrib.png", width=630, height=378, units="px")
ggp
dev.off()

# add legend, things get weird
ggp = ggplot(data=fullmelt, aes(x=date, y=value, color=variable, fill=variable, width=20)) + 
    scale_x_date(expand = c(0, 0)) + 
    xlab("
Source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis") + 
    ylab("$billions 2005 dollars") + 
    theme_bw() +
    layer(data=gdpmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=posmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=negmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    opts(legend.position="top", legend.direction="horizontal", plot.background = theme_rect(colour = 'black', fill = '#CCCCEE', size = 1, linetype='solid')) +
    scale_colour_manual(name="Contributions to GDP", breaks = c("GDPC96","PCECC96","FPIC96","CBIC96","GCEC96","NETEXC96"), values = c("black", "white","red","green","blue","yellow"),labels = c('GDP','Consumption', 'Fixed Investment','Inventories','Government','Net Exports'))

#output
png(filename="/Temp/contribng.png", width=630, height=378, units="px")
ggp
dev.off()

Druce, 

I'm not sure if I completely understand what you want in the end, but we'll give it a go. 

fill and colour are two different scales and when you are trying to combine them manually into a legend you have to specify them both to be exactly the same to get them to unify. If that was what you were after then I think the following should work (might have to remove breaks put in by gmail). 

Brandon

P.S. White bar + white background = invisible bars.

scale_x_date(expand = c(0, 0)) + 
    xlab("
Source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis") + 
    ylab("$billions 2005 dollars") + 
    theme_bw() +
    layer(data=gdpmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=posmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    layer(data=negmelt,geom="bar", stat='identity', position='stack') +
    opts(legend.position="top", legend.direction="horizontal", plot.background = theme_rect(colour = 'black', fill = '#CCCCEE', size = 1, linetype='solid')) +

scale_colour_manual(name="Contributions to GDP", breaks = c("GDPC96","PCECC96","FPIC96","CBIC96","GCEC96","NETEXC96"), values = c("black", "grey80","red","green","blue","yellow"),labels = c('GDP','Consumption', 'Fixed Investment','Inventories','Government','Net Exports'))+scale_fill_manual(name="Contributions to GDP", breaks = c("GDPC96","PCECC96","FPIC96","CBIC96","GCEC96","NETEXC96"), values = c("black", "grey80","red","green","blue","yellow"),labels = c('GDP','Consumption', 'Fixed Investment','Inventories','Government','Net Exports'))
